items.title: ci: add README test-count drift check (#210)
items.body:
Closes #210

## Summary
Add an automated CI drift check to ensure `README.md` test-count claims (line 14 badge and line 215 code comment) match the runtime collected test count (`uv run pytest --collect-only -q`).

- Added `scripts/check_readme_test_count.py` to parse README counts, recount tests, compare, and report drift with exit code 1 naming both numbers.
- Added CI step `README test-count drift check` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `gate` before slow coverage gates.
- Updated `pyproject.toml` `testpaths` to `["packages", "apps", "tests"]`.
- Added unit tests in `tests/test_readme_drift.py` covering parse logic, error handling, matching success, mismatch failure, and CLI entrypoint.
- Updated `README.md` test counts from `1247` to `1641` (the current ground truth count on `test`).
- Added entry under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Negative Control Evidence (Mandatory)

### 1. Mismatch (Mutated README test count to 999)
- **Command**: `uv run python scripts/check_readme_test_count.py`
- **Exit Code**: `1`
- **Output**:
  ```text
  README test count drift detected!
    Collected count: 1641
    README badge count (line 14): 999
    README comment count (line 215): 999
  ```
- **Verdict**: Step failed as expected and printed BOTH numbers (collected count: 1641, badge count: 999, comment count: 999).

### 2. Restored (Restored README test count to 1641)
- **Command**: `uv run python scripts/check_readme_test_count.py`
- **Exit Code**: `0`
- **Output**:
  ```text
  README test counts match collected pytest total (1641 tests).
  ```
- **Verdict**: Step passed cleanly when README test counts match collected count.

### 3. Regex Parse Verification
- **Line 14 Badge Regex**: `re.search(r"https://img\.shields\.io/badge/tests-(\d+)%20passing", content)` extracted `1641`. Missing badge raises `ValueError("Could not parse test count badge from README.md")`.
- **Line 215 Comment Regex**: `re.search(r"#\s*(\d+)\s+tests\s+\+\s+coverage", content)` extracted `1641`. Missing comment raises `ValueError("Could not parse test count comment from README.md")`.

## Review Verdict
`VERDICT: SHIP`

items.title: docs: guard README's test-count/coverage claim against drift
items.body:
## Summary

README's "## Project status" paragraph states, present-tense, "433 tests at 97% coverage" — but nothing regenerated that sentence, so it silently drifted as the suite grew (currently 501 tests). PR #49 (mutation-testing gate, M8/CQ-47) flagged this exact gap in its own description: *"the README build-blockquote test count is not bumped here ... the M8 auto-stamp backlog item is the systemic fix and remains open."* This PR is that fix.

- **`scripts/check-readme-claims.py`** re-derives both numbers independently — the actual test count via `pytest --collect-only` and the actual coverage total via `coverage report --format=total` — and fails loudly if either differs from README's claim. Same "claims must be regenerable, never hand-typed and stale" discipline `scripts/writeup-check.py` already applies to `docs/writeup/methods.md`, applied here to the README's own gate summary.
- Wired into `make test` (stage 3), immediately after pytest populates `.coverage` for the run, so the figure it checks against is always fresh, not a stale committed artifact (`docs/audits/coverage.xml` is itself gitignored regenerable churn).
- README's claim is updated to the current true numbers (501 tests, 97% coverage) so the new gate starts green.

items.title: chore: harness tests count tokens
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes a regression where `:countTokens` for both Gemini (`generativelanguage`) and Vertex (`aiplatform`) reported only the `contents` token count because `systemInstruction`, `generationConfig`, and `toolConfig` were unconditionally stripped from the request body. In the reported case, a ~7.4k-token system prompt plus tool declarations counted as only 17 tokens on Vertex.

The root cause is that the two endpoints require opposite request shapes:
- **Gemini**: `systemInstruction`, `tools`, `toolConfig`, and `generationConfig` are rejected as `Unknown name` at the top level and must be wrapped inside a `generateContentRequest` envelope. Top-level `contents`/`model` are silently ignored when the envelope is present.
- **Vertex**: These fields are accepted flat; only `toolConfig` (and a few others) must be stripped. There is no envelope.

The `/genai` ingress must now parse both shapes and emit whichever the resolved provider requires. The Bifrost-only `fallbacks` routing field must be honoured for routing but stripped before the upstream call.

## Changes

- Added E2E test suite **34. Gemini/Vertex countTokens full-prompt accounting** covering:
  - **34.1 / 34.6** – Contents-only baseline for Gemini and Vertex respectively, recording `totalTokens` as a collection variable for relative assertions in subsequent cases.
  - **34.2 / 34.7** – Flat `systemInstruction` is counted (not stripped) for both providers.
  - **34.3** – Flat `tools`, `toolConfig`, and `generationConfig` are wrapped into the Gemini envelope rather than forwarded verbatim (which would produce a hard 400).
  - **34.8** – Vertex keeps `tools` and `generationConfig` flat but strips `toolConfig`.
  - **34.4 / 34.9** – A `generateContentRequest` envelope is passed through for Gemini and unwrapped for Vertex.
  - **34.5** – The Bifrost `fallbacks` field is stripped before the upstream call and does not alter the counted token total.
- Assertions are relative (count must exceed the contents-only baseline) rather than absolute, so they remain valid across model version updates. A dropped field collapses the count back to baseline, which is exactly the regression signature these cases catch.
- HTTP 400 is intentionally **not** in the infra guard for the tools/toolConfig/fallbacks cases — a 400 from upstream is itself the regression signature for those scenarios.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Affected areas

- [x] Providers/Integrations

## How to test

Import the updated `provider-harness.json` collection into Postman or Newman and run group **34** with valid `genaiKey`, `genaiModel`, `vertexModel`, and `baseUrl` collection variables set.

```sh
newman run tests/e2e/api/collections/provider-harness.json \
  --folder "34. Gemini/Vertex countTokens full-prompt accounting (PR #5620)" \
  --env-var baseUrl=<your-base-url> \
  --env-var genaiKey=<your-api-key> \
  --env-var genaiModel=gemini-2.5-pro \
  --env-var vertexModel=gemini-2.5-pro
```

Each case should return HTTP 2xx with `totalTokens` strictly greater than the baseline recorded in 34.1/34.6. Any case that returns an `Unknown name` error or a token count equal to the baseline indicates the regression has re-appeared.

## Breaking changes

- [x] No

Closes #5620

## Security considerations

No auth, secrets, or PII changes. Test requests use a scoped no-op tool declaration (`probe_context`) with no real side effects.

## Summary

- document the `v0.1.0-beta.1` installation routes: a macOS Apple Silicon preview when published or an Apache-2.0 source build
- describe State v2 queue persistence, separate engine-session authority, evidence-dependent Resume and Retry, conservative recovery, destination reservations, and backend-authorized actions
- state the exact `youtube_dlp v0.2.0`, Go 1.25.12, Node.js 22, Wails v2.13.0, external FFmpeg/FFprobe, checksum, manual-update, privacy, and package boundaries
- include four verified 2560×1600 lifecycle screenshots using Blender Foundation open-movie media
- link the architecture, release, contribution, license, and attribution documentation

## Rationale

The repository needs an accurate landing page for its first beta. This README limits every product and distribution claim to implemented behavior and the supported macOS Apple Silicon package scope.

## Validation

- `npm ci`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run test:ui`
- `npm run build`
- `go mod tidy -diff`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -count=1 ./...`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- `go build ./...`
- tracked Markdown link validation
- PNG type and 2560×1600 dimension checks
- version, unsupported-claim, and security-bypass wording scans
- `git diff --check`

## Limitations

- packaged preview scope is macOS Apple Silicon only
- FFmpeg and FFprobe are external requirements
- updates are manual
- Resume and Retry reuse retained bytes only when the engine validates the session evidence
- playlists, channels, search, Shorts, live streams, authenticated downloads, other sites, DRM decryption, and broad yt-dlp parity are outside the supported application scope
